comment: The console has TWO interfaces and switches between them whenever the cable is plugged or pulled: ethernet d8:e2:df:92:a9:93 (192.168.2.172, static reservation dhcp.@host[1]) and WiFi d8:e2:df:92:a9:90 (192.168.2.169, DYNAMIC lease - no reservation, so this address can change). Both were confirmed on the router 2026-09-15. The firewall rule names EVERY mac in 'interfaces', because a rule naming only one matches nothing while the console is on the other and the block would silently fail open (REVIEW.2 G-02). Accounting resolves the live address at run time from the lease and neighbour tables rather than trusting 'ipv4' here. The top-level 'mac'/'ipv4' keys are legacy aliases for interfaces[0] and are not used when 'interfaces' is present.

router._comment: ubus_path_candidates was trimmed to the one path that answers: /cgi-bin/luci/rpc/ubus is luci-mod-rpc, a different API, and 404s here. tls_sha256 is set by './xbox.py pin'.

state._comment: 'up' means the console's outbound byte rate exceeded threshold_bytes_per_min since the previous sample. CALIBRATED 2026-09-15 against the real console: idle 20.8 KB/min, downloading 93.7 KB/min, gaming 289.5 KB/min outbound - so 200 KB/min separates play from download with 3.1x margin. Bytes come from conntrack accounting, accumulated router-side into a monotonic total; nft counters cannot be used because this router offloads flows in hardware and they would never see the traffic (REVIEW.2 G-01/G-04). A sample older than max_sample_age_s is discarded as stale rather than averaged over the gap.

rules.description: Firewall uci sections named kidsout_xbox* belong to kidsout. block/allow only toggle their 'enabled' option: enabled=1 means the REJECT rule is in force (internet blocked), enabled=0 means it is absent (internet allowed). The single rule lists every console MAC via src_mac, which fw4 parses as a list. Nothing else on the router is touched.
